title: Dimension of a constructible subset and its closure over a field
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $T$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Let $S\subseteq |T|$ be constructible [def-weil-constructible-subset], and let $\overline S$ be its Zariski closure. Give both subsets the subspace topology [def-kun-subspace-topology] and measure their topological Krull dimensions by [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], with the empty set of dimension $-\infty$. Then
$$ \dim S=\dim\overline S.$$
No assertion of this kind is made for an arbitrary subset of $T$, or for an arbitrary Noetherian scheme not of finite type over a field.

source.place: Tag 00OT, lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-over-field, proof of (1)=(2), where every nonempty open in an irreducible component retains its dimension; consequence for a finite locally closed decomposition of a constructible subset

mathlib_searches.query: The dimension of a constructible subset in an algebraic variety equals the dimension of its closure
For a constructible subset of a finite type scheme over a field, its subspace Krull dimension equals that of its Zariski closure
A finite partition of a constructible subset of an algebraic variety into locally closed strata has dimension the maximum of the dimensions of the strata

from.place: First proof paragraph: “the pullback of a constructible sheaf has support the preimage, of dimension raised by the fibre dimension $d$”; justifies replacing the possibly nonclosed support by its closure before applying the smooth local dimension formula.
